**Other information:**

`Clear.getHiddenState()` turned `0` into `'0'` so that it counts as a value, but the return statement then checked `field.value` (still `0`, which is falsy), so a zero hid the clear button. It now checks the local `value`.

New spec: `test/playwright/unit/form/field/trigger/Clear.spec.mjs` covers NumberField `5`, `0`, `7`, `null` and TextField `''`, `'x'`. The `Neo.main.DomEvents` stub is installed in `beforeAll` only if missing and removed in `afterAll`.

Spec written first; failing output before the fix:

```
1) [unit-engine] › test\playwright\unit\form\field\trigger\Clear.spec.mjs:49:9 › Neo.form.field.trigger.Clear › NumberField value 0 => clear trigger hidden: false

   Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality

   Expected: false
   Received: true

     53 |             field.value = value;
     54 |
   > 55 |             expect(trigger.getHiddenState()).toBe(hidden);
        |                                              ^

  1 failed
  5 passed (900ms)
```

After the fix:
- `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/form/field/trigger/Clear.spec.mjs`: 6 passed.
- `npm run test-unit` (Windows 11): 51 failed, 4506 passed. The same 51 also fail without this change (52 then, the extra one being the `0` row). None are in `form/`; they are in build scripts, git hooks, symlink and packaging specs. Relying on CI for the full-suite result.
- Checked in the browser: `examples/form/field/number/` with `clearToOriginalValue` unticked. A value of `0` now keeps the ✕ visible, and clicking it clears the field.
